answer: Continuous proof-of-work challenge: each identity must solve a fresh computational puzzle (e.g., 2^28 hash iterations) whose answer is a whisper relayed only to the next challenger, so an attacker cloning identities must independently recompute every puzzle, costing roughly 30 CPU-minutes per identity. The vine of prior challenge answers links each new identity to a verified predecessor, and any fork produces a spiral of mismatched hashes that peers reject. Each additional sybil thus pays the full compute cost serially, with no volume discount.
